summary: A waiting issue that Dispatch moves to done, backlog, icebox, or triage now leaves the admission queue and loses its queued tree record in the same durable event step (the new `dequeue` effect, executed by ProcessManager.dequeue before the save); boot (reconcileAdmission) and every resync (sweepStaleQueue) drop stale entries already in the queue with one log line each; a later todo admits the issue again as a fresh root. One predicate, isStaleQueuedStatus in legion-state.ts, decides staleness. PR #1037 at head fb9b26175cfe6667bcae501ad912a4324a151919, CI Tests run 34763882859 green; smoke-rig proof below.

trickyParts: Biome import order is case-insensitive: `staleQueueEntryReason` sorts after `type PendingAssignment` in processes.ts (the plan said after isBystanderRole); `isStaleQueuedStatus` is accepted after `type IssueStatus` in reducers.ts.

The boot sweep must run before the demote/promote loop and after `admission.cap = ...`; the resync sweep after healStatusDrift so the status judged is the one Dispatch reports. Both go through staleQueueEntryReason; the reducers go through dequeueIfWaiting -> isStaleQueuedStatus. `"icebox"` appears in one non-test file only (legion-state.ts).

A queued entry whose issue reads a daemon-owned status (LEGSMOKE-156 in_progress+queued after the first rig boot's launch hold; LEGSMOKE-159 in_progress+queued behind cap 1) is the legitimate shape and was left alone by both sweeps on the rig, as designed.
openQuestions: Box-level, reported to the architect (Envoy 87b44ffc2247a4d031564e5eeec0e068): ~/.omp/natives/18.1.15/pi_natives.linux-x64-modern.node (written 14:54:14Z) carries sentinel __piNativesV18_0_10 while the production pane binary omp-18.1.15-sami.9bff2014-rpcfix demands __piNativesV18_1_15; three 18.1.15 builds share that directory. New production panes from that binary (e.g. this issue's tester) will likely fail at boot until the operator re-syncs; operator-owned shared state, not touched.
testerNotes: Re-run task 8 steps 5-8 at the head under test. On this branch, up.sh's hardcoded NATS container name collides with any sibling rig; run main's scripts/smoke/up.sh+down.sh as a working-copy overlay (jj file show -r main@origin ...) with your own SMOKE_PROJECT/SMOKE_DIR/ports, under `env -u LEGION_OMP_PATH`, and jj restore them afterwards. Dispatch POST/PATCH need `actor: {kind: "session", id, origin}`. The seeded restart needs the two GH_*_APP_PRIVATE_KEY_B64 secrets in the daemon's env (run under `secrets ... --`).

A controller reorder pass (backlog then todo on a queued issue) makes that issue leave and rejoin the queue at the back; sibling rig controllers also triage fresh LEGSMOKE issues within seconds -- not failures.
